AgriFresh Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AgriFresh Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a telephone, or click the raise hand icon if joining via webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AgriFresh Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael Thompson.

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: capital expenditure plans and priorities, key achievements and challenges in the quarter, progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, organic revenue growth overall and by region, performance of key brands and product categories, and impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue.

On capital expenditures, we're ramping up investments to build resilience and growth capacity. Regarding achievements and challenges, we navigated input costs and disruptions while hitting growth milestones. Sustainability remains central, with solid progress on sourcing and emissions. Organically, we grew across regions through volumes and premium mix. Our brands shone in beverages, snacks, and health categories. Finally, FX was a headwind we mitigated effectively.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Michael. As Michael mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $2.48 billion, representing an 8.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 34.7%, impacted by persistent input cost inflation in dairy, sugar, and oils, partially offset by pricing and productivity. Operating income was $312 million, and earnings per share were $0.87. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Before we get into questions, let me expand on those six areas Michael highlighted, starting with our capital expenditure plans and priorities for fiscal 2025, as outlined in our earnings supplement on page 17. CapEx is foundational to driving margin expansion, supply chain strength, and share gains in high-growth areas like plant-based proteins, functional beverages, and ready-to-eat snacks.

For FY25, we're targeting $850 million in total CapEx, or about 4.2% of projected net sales—up 12% from $760 million last year. This reflects optimism on consumer demand as inflation eases. We've averaged 3.8% of sales over five years, yielding 18% IRR historically, and expect at least 20% IRR ahead, focused on projects paying back in under 24 months.

By category, per the pie chart on slide 18, manufacturing and capacity get $375 million, or 44%, up from 38%. This includes $150 million for three new aseptic filling lines in Modesto, California, and Querétaro, Mexico, expanding ready-to-drink functional beverage capacity 25% for low-sugar, high-protein shakes like our VitaBoost line, up 28% YoY in Q4. These Krones servo-driven fillers reduce downtime 30% and improve accuracy to ±0.5 grams, similar to PepsiCo's Prime investments.

Supply chain and logistics modernization takes $200 million, or 24%, informed by past disruptions. With ocean freight inflation now mid-single digits, $80 million goes to automated high-bay warehousing with AS/RS at Memphis, tied to our SAP S/4HANA upgrade, aiming for 10x inventory turns and 98% OTIF. North America gets 55%, with dual-sourcing against port risks; EMEA $40 million for cold-chain retrofits meeting EU Farm-to-Fork regs, cutting Scope 3 emissions 15% via Phaseout-ready refrigerants.

Sustainability allocates $140 million, or 16%, supporting our 2030 net-zero goal. $60 million for solar-plus-storage microgrids at five plants, covering 40% of U.S. energy and trimming power costs 12%, like Nestlé's approach. $30 million for reverse osmosis and zero-liquid-discharge in India and Brazil beverage ops. $50 million for lightweight PET recycling lines enables 100% rPET snacks by Q3 '25, cutting virgin resin 35% amid 20%+ PET volatility, as 62% of Gen Z prioritizes this per Nielsen.

Digital transformation: $85 million, or 10%, with $40 million in Siemens MindSphere AI predictive maintenance across 15 plants, targeting 25% less unplanned downtime amid 6% labor cost rises. IoT on Tetra Pak lines boosts yields for premium oat milk like PureOat, with 15% OEE gains in pilots.

Retail and innovation centers: $50 million, or 6%, including $25 million for five D2C stores in Chicago and São Paulo for NPD acceleration. Atlanta's SnackLab targets upcycled protein bars in the $12 billion U.S. market at 7% CAGR.

Regionally: U.S./Canada 48% or $410 million for at-home snacking; EMEA 28% or $235 million for compliance and premiumization; APAC 18% or $155 million for urbanization-driven beverages; LatAm 6% or $50 million for ag resilience.

These build our moat amid consolidation, expanding margins 150 bps, ROIC to 15% by FY26, with 70/30 maintenance/growth split. $600 million green bonds at 3.8% fund sustainable parts. Focused on resilience, sustainability, and adjacencies like RTD coffee and plant-based snacks, targeting 8-10% EPS growth.

Next, key achievements and challenges in the quarter highlight our portfolio's resilience. Net revenues hit $2.48 billion, up 8.2% or 6.1% organically excluding FX and M&A. Adjusted EBITDA was $412 million at 16.6% margin, up 110 bps from pricing, mix, and productivity.

Achievements: Balanced growth in Beverages (42% of revenues, +10.3% organic to $1.04 billion) via ZestQuench low-cal soda gaining 2.1 share points, Refresh Redefined campaign upping penetration 4.7%, and premium sparkling/functional up 18% in clubs. Snacks & Confectionery (+7.5% to $850 million) with NutriCrunch in 5,000 more Walmart doors, +9.2% volume, 25% less sodium chips, margins +240 bps to 38.2% from $28 million Supply Chain 2.0 savings. Health & Nutrition (+12.8% to $590 million) led by VitalFuel plant-based bars +22%, APAC +16% via e-com.

Operationally: Three solar facilities cut Scope 1 emissions 18%; blockchain for 65% cocoa amid 22% price spikes; D2C NutriHub +35% to $120 million. North America 62% of growth, +1.2 share; LatAm +14%; APAC +11%.

Challenges: Input inflation (dairy +11%, sugar +9%, oils +15%) compressed gross margin 80 bps before 5.2% pricing, with 1.8% indulgent volume dip. Freight delays added $12 million; EMEA +2.1% hit by macro and regs; value segments -4%; SG&A +50 bps to 12.4% for Health Forward launches.

This affirms Balanced Growth 2025: 40% premiumization, D2C to 10%, 200 bps EBITDA expansion, $250 million R&D. Buffers and hedges mitigate risks. Full-year: 7-9% organic, 16.5-17% margins.

On progress with sustainability initiatives and goals, it's core to value creation amid 78% consumer ESG preference and regs like EU CSRD and CA SB 253. Pillars: sourcing, water, packaging, net-zero.

Sustainable sourcing: 92% priority commodities responsibly (vs. 82% YoY, ahead of 85% '25 target). 100% RA cocoa for Harvest Bites; 88% RSPO palm oil avoiding 150,000 tons deforestation; 95% Fairtrade arabica. LatAm 98% blockchain-traced; SE Asia NDPE-compliant. Unlocks $45 million retailer incentives.

Water stewardship: 28% intensity reduction since 2020 (beat 20% '25 goal); absolute -15% to 1.2B m3. Memphis 95% reuse; India 120% basin replenishment.

Packaging: 87% recyclable/compostable (+10 pts); 35% PCR, diverting 240,000 tons virgin. Europe 94% PPWD-compliant; NA Project STOP 5,000 tons cleaned. Enzymatic depoly for 50% PCR by '27.

Net-zero: Scope 1/2 -32%; 65% renewables via 200MW Texas PPA. Scope 3 intensity -18%; 78% Tier 1 SBTi; 450,000 acres regen ag sequestering 120,000 tCO2e.

Accretive: 4% revenue from Harvest Green (+220 bps margins); avoided $65 million taxes. 2.5% sales CapEx, $180 million FY25 green tech.

We're outpacing goals for $1.3T opportunities.

Organic revenue growth was 7.2% overall—beating 5-6% guide, ahead of 3-4% industry—our sixth accelerating quarter: 3.8% volume, 2.1% pricing, 1.3% mix (7.8% underlying).

SKU rationalization cut low-velocity 15%; ZestQuench at 18% sales; AI forecasting +22% turns, -35% stockouts; rPET loyalty +12 NPS.

By region: NA (42%) +9.1% (NutriCrunch +110 bps share, ElectraSport +28%, e-com +15%). EMEA (28%) +6.4% (VitaBloom +22%, precision ferm -18% costs). APAC (18%) +8.9% (FizzPure +32%, Koru seltzers). LATAM (12%) +4.8% (AquaVida impulse, solar hubs -14% logistics).

On track 6.5-7.5% full-year; Q4 +2% volume.

Key brands and categories grew 8.2% organic, beating 3.5% industry: 4.1% volume, 2.7% pricing, 1.4% mix.

Beverages (42%) +9.1%: AquaPure +12.3% (95% ACV); FizzCore flat but zero-sugar +18%; VitaBoost +22.4% esports. Snacks (28%) +7.6%: CrunchMax +11.2% flavors; NutriTrail +9.8%. Dairy/Alts (18%) +6.9%: CoreDairy +10.1%; GreenWave +28.7% oat yogurt. Health (12%) +15.4%: ImmunoBoost +32%, KetoCore +41%.

NA 10.3%; EMEA 4.2%; APAC 14.7%. $150 million digitization +22% accuracy; regen nuts -12% Scope 3; Focus 2025 divests $300 million for $500 million R&D.

FX impact: $150 million headwind; reported +4%, constant +7%, organic constant 6%. NA minor CAD drag. EMEA $85 million EUR -8%. APAC JPY tailwind offset IDR/PHP. LATAM $10 million BRL/MXN tailwind.

YTD $420 million headwind like peers. 75% hedged (forwards, collars, natural); local-for-local Poland plant; 4-6% pricing recouped 60%. FY headwind 2-3%.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 7-9% organic growth and 16.5-17% EBITDA margins.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation remained a challenge, with dairy up 11%, sugar 9%, and oils 15%, compressing margins 80 basis points before our 5.2% pricing actions clawed back 70%. We saw some elasticity in indulgent snacks with a 1.8% volume dip, similar to peers, but premium categories held strong. Our productivity and hedging kept us resilient.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for new products and what is the expected impact?

Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. We're excited about our Q4 launches, including zero-sugar energy shots and upcycled protein bars from SnackLab. These target the $12 billion bar market and functional RTD space, expecting 12-15% category growth, adding 1-2 points to organic revenue via premiumization and e-com acceleration to 10% of sales.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

David Lee (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. We've invested $200 million in modernization, like AS/RS warehousing for 98% OTIF and multi-sourcing against Red Sea and port risks. Blockchain covers 65% cocoa, and solar microgrids enhance resilience. Delays were limited to under two weeks, adding just $12 million, with inventory buffers and hedges covering 70% commodities.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Sarah Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thanks, Sarah. Q4 should see 2% volume acceleration from holidays and launches, sustaining 6.5-7.5% organic. FX eases to 2-3% headwind, CapEx drives efficiency for margin expansion, and sustainability fuels premium growth. We're positioned for 8-10% EPS through the cycle.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Michael Thompson for closing remarks.

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in AgriFresh Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
